title: Prevent sub-second metering retries from generating duplicated invoice line artifacts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: We are seeing a class of invoice inaccuracies caused by sub-second metering retries: when the ingestion pipeline receives near-duplicate usage pulses within <1s (retries or multi-scribe clients), the export reconciler sometimes persists both pulses, leading to duplicated invoice lines or misapportioned proration for reserved capacity and burst credits. This ticket implements a defensive layer in the billing export path to suppress near-duplicate pulses and provide deterministic export signatures.

Background and impact: Over the last two months the export anomaly detector has flagged a ~0.4% spike in invoice line deltas tied to very short latency duplicate events. Affected customers see small but material overcharges or unexpected negative adjustments when downstream compensations run. The issue is high customer impact for enterprise tenants on heavy rate-limit/burst traffic patterns.

Root cause hypothesis: The metering ingestion is eventually consistent across collectors. Retries or duplicate client writes can produce pulses with identical user_id, meter_id, interval_start within the same second but slightly different metadata (trace_id). The export pipeline groups by epoch bucket boundaries at 1-second resolution for performance; however, the export line generator lacks an in-process de-duplication guard and can emit two export lines that later pluralize into invoice differences after proration logic.

Proposed solution: 1) Add a lightweight idempotency/dedup filter in the export leader that canonicalizes pulses by (tenant_id, meter_key, bucket_epoch_seconds, rounded_quantity) and drops duplicates when there is a matching recent fingerprint. 2) Persist an export-fingerprint along with export manifest records to ensure downstream idempotency when replays/backfills occur. 3) Adjust proration logic to treat suppressed pulses as a single atomic quantity for subsecond windows to avoid fractional rounding oscillation. 4) Add an analytics counter and alert when duplicates are suppressed > 0.1% of incoming pulses.

Implementation notes: - Filter will be implemented inside the export leader process (go/runtime/exporter) to avoid cross-leader coordination. Use a local LRU+TTL cache keyed by fingerprint with TTL = 5 minutes and capacity per-tenant to avoid memory blowup. - Fingerprint form: sha1(tenant_id|meter_key|bucket_epoch_seconds|rounded_quantity) followed by metadata version tag. Store fingerprint as part of export manifest row (export_manifest.fingerprint). - Backfill strategy: existing late-arrival backfill runner will consult export manifests to avoid double-applying suppressed pulses. We'll add a migration job to mark prior exports missing fingerprints as 'legacy' so they remain compatible. - Performance: the fingerprint computation is CPU-light and will be sampled in canary to validate no tail latency impact. - Tests: unit tests for fingerprint collision and end-to-end integration test simulating retry storm and verifying single export line emitted. Add fuzz tests that generate near-duplicate pulses.

Observability and metrics: - New metric: billing.export.duplicate_suppressed_count (per-tenant, per-meter). - Export manifest additions will expose export_manifest.fingerprint and export_manifest.fingerprint_version. - Dashboard: add 'Duplicate suppression' panel to billing/export-anomalies dashboard and alert if suppression rate > 0.1% for >30m. Links: design doc and dashboards in attachments.

Migration and rollout: - Phase 1 (canary): Deploy to export leader subset in us-east-1, sample 5% of tenants, run dedup in probe mode (log intended suppression but do not drop). Validate false positives < 0.01%. Duration 72 hours.
- Phase 2 (soft enforcement): Deploy to 25% export leaders, enable suppression for low-risk tenants, run for 3 days, monitor metrics and invoices for unexpected regressions.
- Phase 3 (global): enable across all leaders with migration job sweeping older exports to tag legacy rows. Backfill/repair runner will identify invoices affected and generate corrective adjustments as needed.

Rollback plan: Remove suppression flag and roll the manifest schema change as a non-destructive toggle. We can replay exports for affected intervals using existing shadow-export runner.

Notes and risks: - TTL for fingerprint cache must be tuned: too short -> duplicates may still slip through; too long -> undercounting legitimate distinct pulses across real intervals. We will tune based on production distribution sampling. - Edge case: very-high-frequency legitimate pulses (subsecond bursts from real workloads) may be collapsed; we will expose an allowlist for tenants known to generate legitimate subsecond pulses (rare). - Must coordinate with accounting and billing teams for any invoice adjustments; they should be notified before global rollout.

Owner: Billing infra; contact: maya.chen@redwood.ai and liam.oconnor@redwood.ai
comments: 2025-02-13 - Maya Chen: Initial triage completed. Scoped local fingerprint cache approach; added perf guard rails. Created design doc (attached).

2025-02-17 - Infrastructure review: CPU sampling during an offline run showed <0.7% CPU increase at 99th percentile for exporter process on t3a.large equivalent. Recommended canary. - reviewer: Priya Nair
2025-02-21 - PM note (Jordan Fisk): Coordinate with Finance and Support to prepare communication template for any customer-facing price adjustments if backfills are necessary.
2025-02-25 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented filter in go/runtime/exporter; added unit tests. Opened PR for manifest schema change. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4521

2025-03-01 - QA: Integration test harness ran against simulated retry-storm dataset; single export line emitted in 98/100 runs. Two failures investigated (edge-case with exact quantity drift) - fixing rounding normalization. - QA owner: Alex Rivera
2025-03-03 - Rollout plan updated: include tenant allowlist and a 'probe' mode for 7 days instead of 3 for slower detection of invoice drift.
